enable_auth_method.note: Creates an OAuth/OIDC source (external IdP). Also used for SAML sources via /api/v3/sources/saml/.

create_organization.note: Creates an OAuth2/OIDC provider (not an organization). Mapped to create_organization for compatibility with the canonical ops vocabulary.

saml.description: SAML sources can allow IdP-initiated logins, and the documentation explicitly warns this may be a security risk because the request is not verified.
saml.note: Acceptance of unsolicited SAML responses in this mode is configuration-dependent and should not be treated the same as failure of SP-initiated request correlation.

saml.description: Administrators can reconfigure providers and sources, including certificates and issuer settings, and the new trust configuration is expected to take effect.
saml.note: Acceptance under newly configured trust material is by design after an admin change.

saml.description: Applications are accessible to all users when no policy/group/user bindings are defined.
saml.note: Successful access without bindings is by design and must not be flagged as authorization bypass.

saml.description: When an OAuth/OIDC client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested.
saml.note: Tests for least privilege must request explicit narrow scopes; otherwise broader claims are by design.

saml.description: SAML NameID value is derived from configured/default NameID policy and may be hashed ID, distinguishedName, UPN, session ID, or email address.
saml.note: Identity string differences across logins may reflect configured NameID derivation rather than principal confusion.

saml.description: When a Source stage resume timeout is exceeded, the suspended flow restarts from the beginning on return from the external source.
saml.note: A restarted flow after timeout is documented behavior, not a session-binding bug.

saml.description: Administrative session deletion, user deactivation, token revocation, or expiration trigger SLO/back-channel logout to configured providers.
saml.note: Downstream logout after admin-authorized termination is by design.

saml.description: If a source authentication or enrollment flow contains a User Login stage, the original flow is not resumed and the pending user is authenticated directly.
saml.note: This is documented behavior of Source stage composition and can invalidate resume-based tests.

saml.description: OAuth access tokens are bearer credentials used to call protected APIs such as userinfo until expiry or revocation.
saml.note: Reuse of a valid bearer token across multiple API calls is expected unless a one-time artifact is explicitly documented.

saml.description: A valid unexpired bearer access token can be reused across multiple API calls.
saml.source: RFC 6750 / authentik OAuth token usage docs
saml.note: Do not flag ordinary bearer token reuse as replay unless the artifact is documented as one-time.

saml.description: The nbf claim is optional and lack of enforcement is spec-compliant.
saml.note: Do not treat acceptance without nbf enforcement as a vulnerability by itself.

saml.description: As of authentik 2025.10, the email scope defaults email_verified to False because authentik has no authoritative verification source.
saml.note: Do not flag email_verified=false as a bug on current versions; older versions differed.

saml.constraint: SAML login testing against authentik as SP MUST use POST to /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/ with form fields SAMLResponse and RelayState, and MUST initiate the SP flow first so the forged response carries a matching InResponseTo. Sending a fabricated ACS POST without first starting the flow will be rejected for flow-state reasons, not because the security check under test worked.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution default-config testing on SAML Source, the fuzzer MUST explicitly create the SAML source with default settings and set Allow IDP-Initiated Logins only if the test intends to exercise unsolicited assertions. The documentation states Allow IDP-Initiated Logins may constitute a security risk because the request is not verified; acceptance in that mode is not evidence that SP-initiated request validation is broken.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, configure the SAML source with an explicit upstream Issuer/Entity ID and then send a mismatched assertion Issuer. If the source is created without a concrete issuer binding, an issuer-mismatch test can become inconclusive because the expected issuer trust anchor was never pinned.

For I2 replay and expiry tests on SAML assertions, include a CONTROL login with a valid assertion before the mutated assertion. Without a successful control, rejection of the attack assertion cannot be distinguished from broken source configuration, bad ACS flow state, or malformed SAML construction.

Allow IDP-Initiated Logins on a SAML source is documented as a security risk because the request is not verified. The fuzzer MUST treat acceptance of unsolicited IdP-initiated login as a configuration-dependent behavior, not as proof that SP-initiated request correlation is broken. Use this setting only when intentionally testing IdP-initiated behavior.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving Source stage resume, the source stage Resume timeout can cause the suspended original flow to restart from the beginning after return from the external source. A valid coherence test MUST keep the external round-trip within the configured resume timeout; otherwise a restarted flow is by design, not a session-binding failure.

For I3 tests involving policies on flows or stage bindings, authentik supports two evaluation modes: Evaluate when flow is planned and Evaluate when stage is run. The fuzzer MUST keep this mode fixed during a test and interpret results accordingly. A policy evaluated at plan time can legitimately use earlier context than one evaluated at stage-run time; differing outcomes across those modes are configuration semantics, not necessarily coherence bugs.

For I3 config-change tests on logout/session invalidation, authentik documents that administrative session deletion, user deactivation, token revocation, or expiration legitimately trigger SLO/back-channel logout. Do NOT flag downstream logout after such admin action as a coherence violation; it is by design session termination.

For I4 principal-binding tests on SAML, NameID format materially changes the identifier value. Persistent NameID uses a hashed user ID, transient uses the session ID, emailAddress uses the user's email, and other formats may fall back to persistent identifiers. The fuzzer MUST hold NameID policy constant across compared logins; otherwise identity differences may be caused by configured NameID derivation rather than collision or merge bugs.

Email-based NameID is documented as unsafe for stable identity because users may change email addresses. For I4 tests, do NOT assume email NameID is a persistent principal identifier. If the source or provider is configured to use email-based NameID, account-linking and collision results must be interpreted as email-derived behavior, not stable-subject semantics.

For I4 tests involving source-based account linking or enrollment through a Source stage, the source's authentication/enrollment flows MUST NOT contain a User Login stage. The documentation states this prevents resuming the original flow and instead directly authenticates the pending user. If present, identity outcomes are confounded by flow design rather than principal-binding logic.

For I5 authorization tests on applications, authentik applications are allow-all by default when no bindings are defined. The fuzzer MUST bind a policy, group, or user when it expects denial behavior. Otherwise successful access may simply reflect the documented default-open application access model, not an authorization bypass.

For I5 scope/claim tests using OAuth endpoints after SAML-related setup, when a client requests no scopes authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. The fuzzer MUST explicitly request the intended scopes; omitting scope broadens claims by design and can create false positives for over-grant.

For I5 tests involving redirect URI validation on OAuth/OIDC applications used alongside SAML setups, authentik allows regex redirect URIs. The fuzzer MUST distinguish exact redirect URI entries from regex-based entries; broad regex acceptance is admin-configured behavior and not evidence of token audience or authorization over-grant by itself.

Numeric sentinel analysis: User Login stage Session duration defaults to a browser-session cookie when set to seconds=0. Do NOT interpret 0 as immediate expiry. Value 0 means 'expire when browser session ends' rather than zero-second invalidation.

Numeric sentinel analysis: User Login stage Stay signed in offset uses seconds=0 as the default disabled state for the extra prompt. Do NOT assume 0 means an immediate extension window; it means the stay-signed-in extension prompt is not offered.

Numeric sentinel analysis: Authenticator Validation stage Last validation threshold uses non-zero to enable less-frequent MFA validation. A zero value means validate every time, not 'no validation'. For code-based devices, values lower than seconds=30 cannot be used reliably due to timestamp granularity.

SAML login testing against authentik as SP MUST use the ACS endpoint /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/ with HTTP POST form fields SAMLResponse and RelayState. The executor MUST initiate the SP flow first so the forged response carries the expected InResponseTo value.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature tests, authentik documentation states SAML sources support signed requests and rely on configured certificates. The fuzzer MUST create a SAML source with explicit trust material/certificate configuration where available; otherwise a successful forged login may reflect incomplete setup rather than signature bypass.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch, the SAML source has an explicit Issuer/Entity ID setting. The fuzzer MUST configure the expected IdP entity ID and then mutate the assertion Issuer. If issuer is left unset or loosely configured, acceptance of a mismatched Issuer is not a valid finding.

For I5 saml_no_audience_restriction and saml_wrong_audience, the SAML source/provider setup MUST include a concrete SP issuer/entity ID and ACS context. Without a configured audience target, acceptance of missing or wrong AudienceRestriction cannot be interpreted reliably.

For I2 replay and expiry tests on SAML assertions, the fuzzer MUST include a control login with a valid assertion before the mutated assertion. Otherwise a failed attack login may be caused by broken source configuration, missing certificates, or flow misconfiguration rather than freshness enforcement.

Source stage resume behavior is time-bound: if the configured Resume timeout is exceeded, the suspended flow restarts from the beginning. Any I3 multi-step coherence test involving embedded SAML/OAuth sources MUST keep the round-trip within the resume timeout or failures will be by design.

Flows and stage bindings in authentik can evaluate policies either when the flow is planned or when the stage is run. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish these modes: a change observed only across a new flow plan after admin reconfiguration is by design, not stale-session inconsistency.

The Source stage documentation explicitly warns that the source's authentication/enrollment flows must NOT contain a User Login stage, otherwise the original flow will not resume and the pending user is directly authenticated. Any SAML source test using a Source stage MUST avoid User Login in the source flow or results are invalid.

NameID handling is configurable and may derive from hashed ID, distinguishedName, UPN, transient session ID, or email address depending on NameID policy and mappings. For I4 principal-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST know which NameID policy is configured; comparing raw sent identifiers to granted identities without accounting for this derivation will cause false positives.

Email-address NameID is explicitly discouraged because users may change email addresses. If a test configures email-based NameID, identity merges or changes tied to email are potentially by configuration design and must not be treated as unexpected principal collapse without additional evidence.

Application access in authentik is allow-all when no bindings are defined. For I5 authorization tests, the fuzzer MUST bind a restricting policy/group/user to the application under test; otherwise successful access may simply reflect the documented default-open application behavior.

OAuth/OIDC redirect URI validation in authentik supports exact URLs and regex patterns. For any SAML profile step that later uses OAuth endpoints for verification or token handling, the fuzzer MUST avoid overbroad regex redirect URIs during security tests because acceptance may be due to intentionally broad admin configuration.

When no OAuth scopes are requested, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. Any verification step using /application/o/userinfo/ or token-based identity checks MUST request explicit minimal scopes, otherwise extra claims may appear by design and mimic I5 over-granting.

offline_access is required to receive refresh tokens starting with authentik 2024.2. Tests that expect refresh_token issuance or revocation MUST request offline_access explicitly; absence of a refresh token is otherwise by design.

The User Login stage uses a duration sentinel where Session duration seconds=0 means browser-session cookie expiry, not immediate invalidation. Do NOT interpret 0 as zero-second rejection in freshness tests.
The User Login stage uses a duration sentinel where Stay signed in offset seconds=0 means the stay-signed-in prompt is disabled. Do NOT treat 0 as an immediate-expiry value.

The Authenticator Validation stage uses a duration sentinel where Last validation threshold of 0 means MFA is required every time; any non-zero value enables reuse within that window. For MFA-related SAML bypass tests, 0 is the strict setting, not disablement.
Email Authenticator Setup uses Token Expiration in minutes with a documented default of 30 when not overridden. Omitting the field does not mean zero-minute validity; it selects the platform default.

SAML testing against authentik as SP MUST use POST to /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/ with form fields SAMLResponse and RelayState. The executor MUST initiate the SP flow first so the forged response can carry the expected InResponseTo value.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution default-config testing, the SAML Source documentation explicitly warns that enabling 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' may be a security risk because the request is not verified. Tests for insecure defaults MUST distinguish IdP-initiated acceptance from normal SP-initiated ACS validation.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, configure the SAML source with an explicit Issuer/Entity ID and compare against the assertion Issuer. If the source is configured loosely or allows IdP-initiated logins, acceptance may reflect missing request binding rather than issuer confusion.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay tests, use TWO saml_login submissions to the same ACS endpoint with the same Assertion/@ID. SAML assertions are not bearer JWTs here; replay detection is expected in SAML contexts and should be tested as stateful behavior.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion tests, include a CONTROL SAML login first using the same source and valid assertion timing. Without a successful control, rejection of the expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken source/provider setup.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving Source stage resume, note that the Source stage suspends the current flow and resumes it later, and Resume timeout controls how long the suspended flow is saved. If the timeout is exceeded, the flow restarts from the beginning BY DESIGN. Do NOT flag restart-after-timeout as a coherence bug.

For I3 tests involving SAML source flows embedded via Source stage, the source's authentication/enrollment flows MUST NOT contain a User Login stage. Documentation states this causes the source flow to authenticate directly instead of resuming the original flow, which would invalidate multi-step coherence tests.

For I3 config-change sequences involving flow policy evaluation, authentik supports two modes: evaluate when flow is planned and evaluate when stage is run. A valid coherence test MUST account for this documented behavior; differences caused solely by planned-vs-runtime policy evaluation are configuration-driven, not necessarily stale-state bugs.

For I4 SAML identity-binding tests, NameID is documented as an identifier used for identification in the assertion and may be persistent, transient, email-based, UPN-based, distinguishedName-based, or hashed ID depending on NameID policy and mappings. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume NameID equals email or username unless the source/provider mapping explicitly sets that.

For I4 email-binding collision tests, avoid treating email-based NameID as a stable principal by default. Documentation explicitly warns that email-based NameID is risky because users may change email addresses. If a test uses email as the asserted identifier, record that this is an admin-selected mapping choice, not a platform-wide invariant.

For I4 multi-identity tests against SAML source, the documentation does not describe wildcard or regex matching semantics for NameID policy, issuer/entity ID, or source slug constraints. Treat these as exact configuration values only; do NOT use '*' expecting wildcard behavior.

For I5 authorization-binding tests on OAuth/OIDC tokens issued after SAML login, remember that when no scopes are requested, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. Tests that intend to verify least-privilege MUST explicitly request a narrow scope set; omitting scope broadens claims by design.

For I5 tests involving email_verified after SAML-to-OIDC flows, authentik documentation states that as of 2025.10 email_verified defaults to False, while prior releases always set it to True for the email scope. This version-dependent behavior MUST be accounted for to avoid false positives in account-linking or authorization tests.
For OIDC verification after SAML login, session_token MUST be the OAuth access_token returned by /application/o/token/, not any id_token. UserInfo uses the bearer access token.

Authorization code values at /application/o/token/ are documented as single-use and short-lived. Reuse of the same code should be tested as anti-replay for code exchange, but not confused with bearer access-token reuse semantics.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
